title: [CQ-V03] Authenticated observation ingestion
description:
Objective: Derive trusted runner identity from protected channel and keep ordinary reports diagnostic.

Deliverable: Authenticated observation ingestion. This is task V03 of the approved full CQ rollout; consume this contract, not the whole reference document.

Scope boundaries: implement this behavior and its regression tests only. Later activation, other platform/client consumers and other task behaviors remain out of scope unless named here. Approved full CQ-01–CQ-08 rollout from the interactive implementation plan (2026-10-24). CQ-01 is already landed. Use original Moe source; daemon owns state, wrappers own host Git writes. User selected Moe-provisioned LOCAL Linux VMs (not cloud CI), coding/QA and checks isolated, and exact designated LOCAL BRANCH delivery. Strong profile stays disabled until isolation, evidence and client gates pass. Preserve legacy behavior and existing dirty bytes. Never directly edit .moe. No second revision authority, scheduler, graph database or native memory database.

Verification command (fresh, exit0 required): cd packages/moe-daemon && npm test

Dependency aliases (wired by Moe task ids after import): V02, R11.
definitionOfDone: Forged runner-observed/source/runnerId arguments do not create trust.
Duplicate observation IDs are idempotent or reject conflicting payloads.
Superseded results cannot retarget candidate/revision; only recorded dispatch recovery is permitted.
Fresh verification `cd packages/moe-daemon && npm test` exits0 and its output is supplied to complete_task.
taskRails: No direct .moe edits; no Git-write commands by agents; wrappers own landing.
Do not enable verified-local or claim isolation until all requisite implementation and certification gates pass.

executionContract.intendedBehavior:
Two new MCP tools are callable ONLY over the authenticated runner channel (CQ-V03a's /runner path, which sets ToolCallContext.runner).
- moe.record_check_dispatch records which check the runner will run. The binding (the task's current candidate, its tree, the approved plan revision, the command and the environment) is pinned while it is current.
- moe.record_check_observation records the single result for a recorded dispatch, with its binding inherited from the dispatch and its runnerId derived from the channel.
- Over /mcp or /ws, each tool refuses with RUNNER_CHANNEL_REQUIRED, and forged runnerId, source or binding arguments are refused by name. A run from moe.record_check_run is never authenticated, so ordinary reports stay diagnostic.
acceptanceCriteria: Forged runner-observed, source and runnerId arguments never create trust. A /mcp call is refused with RUNNER_CHANNEL_REQUIRED, unknown identity or binding keys are refused by name, and a record_check_run run fails isAuthenticatedCheckRun.
A duplicate observation id with an identical payload replays as duplicate:true with no write. A conflicting payload is refused (CHECK_RUN_IMMUTABLE), and a dispatch accepts one observation only.
An observation inherits its candidate and revision from its recorded dispatch, so a superseded dispatch is answered against its own binding and never retargeted. An unrecorded dispatch is refused.
A real /runner WebSocket round trip records an authenticated run, and the same calls over /mcp write nothing.
In a fresh Linux snapshot, `cd packages/moe-daemon && npm test` and `npx tsc --noEmit` both exit 0.
invariants: Without context.runner, nothing is read, validated or written.
No tool argument can set runnerId, source, candidateId, treeSha, command or planRevision on an observation.
record_check_run, checkRunStore and delivery policy (passedOn) are byte-unchanged, so every existing policy result is identical.
The guest bridge allowlist is unchanged, so guests never reach either tool.
compatibility: Existing record_check_run callers (the wrappers' runner-observed reports) keep working and counting exactly as before under the legacy, local-branch, remote-push, merged-pull-request and manual-artifact policies.
CQ-V04 consumes the two tool contracts and isAuthenticatedCheckRun.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
Split, 2026-10-29: the whole of V03 was about 13 files, over the 10-file hard cap. It was cut SPIDR-style:
- V03a (task-3b4e3833), the channel: Interface.
- V03b (task-c9fe2515), the dispatch and observation store: Data.
- This row: the two runner-channel tools plus docs, keeping the original DoD and proving it end to end.
The dependsOn on V02 and R11 is kept as the human instructed. V03a, V03b, C11a and bc8410af were added: the last two edit the same docs, and the epic rail serializes overlapping files.

Channel options considered:
1. Trust a caller-asserted `source: 'runner-observed'`. That is today's behavior, and DoD 1 forbids it.
2. A per-call HMAC. Rejected: the key would still have to be host-held, and signature canonicalization adds risk without adding boundary.
3. OS peer credentials: SO_PEERCRED or named-pipe client PIDs. Rejected as platform-specific.
4. CHOSEN: a host-only key file and a loopback-only `/runner` WebSocket path. Identity is derived at connection time into ToolCallContext.runner. This matches the CQ doc (section 5: the capability sits outside the writer's boundary) and R08 (no daemon token enters a guest).

Why a recorded dispatch: DoD 3 needs one. It pins candidate, tree, approved revision, command and environment WHILE they are current. Observations inherit them, so retargeting is impossible by construction, and recovery means answering a recorded dispatch, even a superseded one.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
- Tool pattern: tools/recordCheckRun.ts, a thin delegate whose store owns every rule; the handler signature is (args, state, context).
- ToolCallContext is in tools/index.ts. McpAdapter builds the context at its invoke site, and WebSocketServer.handleMcpMessage passes the options.
- The guest bridge allowlist in scripts/local-runner/guest-bridge.mjs (TOOLS) forwards no check tool to guests.
- util/daemonGitDocs.test.ts refuses tool descriptions saying the daemon never runs git.
- util/taskTimeBudgetDocs.test.ts matches `### moe.<name>` headings against getTools.
- checkRunStore caps command at 500 characters and planRevision at >= 1. CHECK_OUTCOMES is exported.

- V03b, state/checkObservationStore.ts: recordCheckDispatch(state, runner, {id?, taskId, candidateId, planRevision, command, checkId?, environment}) returning {dispatch, duplicate}.

- The docs are shared with C11a and bc8410af (now dependencies): edit only the new sections and the one sentence.
- Under legacy, a host agent can read the key. That is documented, not fixed here; isolation is R-series work.
